ctgrind.technique: ctgrind (stock valgrind memcheck + VALGRIND_MAKE_MEM_UNDEFINED). Operands are the Phase-18 probe's. Secret limbs are marked undefined AFTER construction via a layout mirror verified from the candidate: d at +0x8, top at +0x10 (BN_num_bits 0x4f9030/0x4f9034). Only d[0..top) is tainted; the pointer and top stay defined, so BN_bin2bn / bn_correct_top artefacts are avoided.

BN_mod_exp_mont_consttime.source_interpretation: src/bn/arith.rs mod_exp_core is a square-and-multiply loop: `if limbs::bit(pd, i) { acc = rem(mul(acc, base), md) }` plus length/bounds checks. The branch on the exponent bit is value-dependent. memcheck cannot separate the bit test from the bit-length/bounds branches because the whole limb array is tainted, so the count of value-dependent sites is at least the loop's bit branch and at most all nine.
BN_mod_exp_mont_consttime.file_line: NOT AVAILABLE. The DSO's .debug_line has 644 CUs (DWARF4) and none maps into mod_exp_core: 0 decoded rows in 0x3e6xxx; `bn/arith.rs` occurs once at file offset 0x6659e7, which is in .rodata (0x621000-0x6b57a3), not .debug_line. addr2line resolves the function name from .symtab but returns ??:0 for the line. DSO offsets and function names are reported instead; no line number is invented.

BN_mod_inverse.source_interpretation: src/bn likely implements the inverse through limbs::mod_inverse with division/remainder, shifts, multiply and subtract. The secret operand drives loop bounds, limb lengths and therefore allocation sizes and memmove lengths. The address-dependent contexts ('Use of uninitialised value of size 8') are secret-derived memory addressing inside div_rem/shl/shr/mul/mod_inverse, not merely taken/not-taken branches.
BN_mod_inverse.file_line: NOT AVAILABLE for the same reason as above; DSO offsets and function names are reported.

non_claims: A dudect t-statistic is not an attack, not a wall-clock claim and not a remote-timing claim; it is a distribution difference at the stated geometry and threshold.
A low t-statistic is not a proof of constant time. The control's low t only validates the instrument at this sensitivity.

ctgrind observes data-flow-dependent branches and address uses only. It does not observe cache behaviour, speculation, port contention or any microarchitectural effect, and it says nothing about data that was not marked undefined.
The Phase-18 2.000x / 4.769x ratios are a bounded work-independence screen, not evidence of the leakage mechanism; the mechanism is the mod_exp_core branch set and the inverse's division/shift work.
The reachability result is static. 'Not reachable by direct/GOT edges' is not 'not reachable in any execution'; the may-bound routes are recorded, and the provider segments were not resolved.
The absence of an ssh/sshd import of either symbol is consistent with the baseline and does not by itself establish unreachability.
The DH path executing mod_exp_core through BN_mod_exp_mont is not a safety or timing result; it is a shared-implementation observation.
No claim is made about any other primitive (RSA-private, EC scalar mul, AEAD tag, HKDF) in this batch.
